fatal_errors: The proposed Mo modification of TiVNbTa does not reconstruct the target comparison between CrFeTaVW and Ta-to-Ti-substituted CrFeTiVW.
The claimed Mo-induced transition to edge-dislocation-controlled strengthening is not established by the cited studies; neither citation isolates a minor Mo addition to TiVNbTa.
The prediction that thermal conductivity will remain essentially unimpaired lacks supporting evidence and does not address the target thermal-diffusivity result.
The falsification rule can reject the performance prediction without testing whether the proposed edge-dislocation mechanism occurred.
explanation: The response presents a testable alloy-design alternative and correctly uses the reported TiVNbTa strengths as its local baseline, but it has little agreement with the hidden study. The target intervention was Ta-to-Ti substitution in CrFeTaVW, evaluated through MD versus hybrid MD/MC, mechanical alloying, SPS, segregation analysis, phase characterization, and thermal diffusivity from 300 to 1000 K. Its mechanism involved thermodynamic atom swapping, W association, Fe–Ta-driven Laves-phase formation, and disorder-limited heat transport. None of these central elements is recovered. Evidence E2 shows edge-dislocation-associated elevated-temperature strength in HfMoNbTaW, but it does not demonstrate that adding 5–10 at.% Mo to TiVNbTa causes the same transition. E1 concerns a different NbMoTaWVTi alloy whose strength also depended on fine grains and TiO precipitation, so it cannot validate retained ductility or conductivity. The composition series and matched processing provide a reasonable performance test, but mechanism falsification would require a predefined observation of dislocation character under comparable deformation conditions, while thermal compatibility would require explicit temperature-dependent diffusivity or conductivity limits and interface-level measurements.
